summary.text: A male dromedary camel calf was born naturally on July 26, 2025 in a rural village north of Wad Ashana city, North Kordofan, Sudan. The owner reported no similar cases in his herd or nearby herds. On examination the calf had complete cardiac displacement outside the thoracic cavity caused by a cleft, with the heart protruding at the most ventral aspect of the cervical region on the left side.

The exposed heart was covered with pericardium and without skin, appeared normal and kept a regular heartbeat. The calf was alert, active and interacted with its mother but was unable to stand for long and suckle. No other congenital abnormalities or malformations were observed.

Supportive care consisted of milking the mother and bottle-feeding colostrum. The calf passed away approximately 2 days after birth. A necropsy was not conducted because of unavailable trained personnel, the long distance to the nearest veterinary hospital and security issues, and the authors suggest the cause of death may have been cardiorespiratory complications and bacterial infections.
